growth_stages.notes: Heat mainly accelerates development rate (shortens duration) rather than directly damaging tissue at this stage.
Most heat-sensitive stage. Pollen viability and grain set are damaged by short heat episodes during meiosis/anthesis.
growth_stages.reference_detail: Grain number most sensitive to heat 300-200 degree-days before flowering at a 28C threshold; a single hot day (30/20C day/night) during meiosis significantly reduces pollen viability.
sources: Girousse et al., Field Crops Research 316 (2024) 109489 - https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378429024002429
Saini & Aspinall 1982, cited in Girousse et al. 2024

growth_stages.notes: Each post-flowering hour above 32C reduces individual grain weight; effect measured 0-500 degree-days after flowering.
growth_stages.reference_detail: Each hour with T>32C post-flowering reduced individual grain weight by ~0.26 mg/spike and grain yield by 2.44 g/m^2 at canopy level.
sources: Girousse et al., Field Crops Research 316 (2024) 109489

engine_notes: Thresholds are peer-reviewed research findings, not FortyGuard-provided or CropHeat-invented values. The 28C/32C figures are field-measured correlations, not universal biological constants -- genotype and local acclimation shift the real threshold.
